plain.text: Adam and Eve had a son, Cain, and later Abel. Abel kept sheep and Cain worked the ground. Cain brought an offering of crops to the LORD, and Abel brought the best portions from the firstborn of his flock. The LORD looked with favour on Abel and his offering, but not on Cain's. Cain was very angry. God said, "Why are you angry? If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must rule over it." Cain said to his brother, "Let's go out to the field," and there he attacked Abel and killed him. The LORD asked, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I don't know," Cain replied. "Am I my brother's keeper?" God said, "Your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground." Cain would be a restless wanderer. Cain said his punishment was more than he could bear, and someone might kill him. So God put a mark on Cain to protect him. Cain went to live in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

Cain had a son, Enoch, and built a city. His descendants included Jabal, the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock; Jubal, the father of musicians; and Tubal-cain, who made tools of bronze and iron. Lamech, another descendant, boasted to his wives that he had killed a man for wounding him, and that he would be avenged seventy-seven times.
Adam and Eve had another son, Seth, since Cain had killed Abel. Seth had a son named Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of the LORD.

summary.bigIdea: Sin grows from envy to murder, yet God warns, protects and gives new beginnings.
points: God warns Cain that sin is crouching at his door and he must master it.
Cain kills his brother Abel and asks, "Am I my brother's keeper?"
People begin to call on the name of the LORD.
summary.reflection: God told Cain that sin was crouching at his door. What helps you master anger or envy before it grows?
